rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notice to quit, grounds for eviction)
rules.requirement: A landlord may remove a tenant only through court process and must have a statutory good cause (e.g., nonpayment, disorderly conduct, lease breach, conversion, owner occupancy). Except for nonpayment, the cause must be described in a written Notice to Quit (and sometimes a Notice to Cease), with notice periods ranging from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground. Lockouts and self-help evictions are illegal.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in document.
rules.exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel/motel guests, transient or seasonal tenants (unless continual residence); units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units
unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rentals including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, and rooming and boarding houses.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years depending on ground
rules.penalty: Illegal self-help eviction: tenant may recover possession and damages, court costs and attorney fees (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1).

parsed.doc_summary: Part 3 of the NJ DCA Landlord-Tenant guide. Most of it covers habitability, heat, lead paint, water testing and remedies, none of which are in scope. The in-scope content is the Anti-Eviction Act: good cause, notice to quit, grounds, exceptions, relocation and self-help prohibition. It is recorded as one just-cause record. The text is cut off partway through ground N.
